concept.title: To-dos: small jobs, kept off the board

conbody.p: A to-do is one paragraph of text: small enough that you just do it and tick it off, like check the wording of REQ-12 or ask Sam about the seal supplier. It has no column, no discussion thread and no agent runs — those are what a board card is for. The board shows only cards, so a list of small asks no longer crowds out the real pieces of work.
A to-do has its text, a tick box (and when it was ticked), who has it, an optional due date, and, when it was raised from a note, a link back to the note's artifact.

section.title: The project's to-do list
section.p: Plan → To-dos is the project's list:

ul.li: Quick add at the top: type the to-do and press Enter. Choose who has it and a due date beside the field if you want to; both are optional.
Tick the box to complete a to-do. Completed to-dos collapse into a Completed line under the list; open it to see them, or untick one to open it again.
Edit changes the text, who has it and the due date. Anything overdue is called out.
Just mine narrows the list to the to-dos assigned to you.
A to-do is one paragraph, at most 1000 characters. Anything longer is a piece of work: put it on the board.

section.title: My to-dos
section.p: My to-dos, the To-dos tab under Plan in the workspace's rail (and linked from every project's To-dos page), gathers your to-dos across the workspace: every to-do assigned to you in a project you can open, each labelled with its project, and your personal to-dos. A personal to-do belongs to no project and nobody else sees it; the quick add on My to-dos makes one.

section.title: Promote to board task
section.p: When a to-do turns out to be bigger than it looked, Promote to board task on its row makes a card of it: the card lands in To Do carrying the to-do's text, who has it, its due date and the artifact it came from. The to-do is ticked off with the note promoted to a board task, which links to the card.

section.title: Raising a to-do from a note
section.p: Mentioning someone with @name in a note on an artifact tells them about it — it does not create work for them. To turn the ask into something tracked, use + Add to-do on the note:

ul.li: Whoever the note names is filled in as the person who has it, and the note's first paragraph as the to-do. Both can be changed, and you can set a due date.
The to-do goes on the project's to-do list, and on the My to-dos of the person who has it, straight away. It does not go on the board.

section.p: Afterwards the note carries a small link to the to-do showing whether it is open or done, so a thread from three weeks ago tells you whether the thing being discussed ever got done, without going to look. The status is read from the to-do each time, not copied.
A note raised before to-dos had a list of their own keeps its link to the board card it raised, and the card stays on the board.
A note can raise one to-do. System and agent entries in the feed do not offer the control: those are a record of what happened, not somebody asking for something.

section.title: For agents
section.p: Agents reach to-dos through the openv tools list_todos, create_todo and tick_todo, so a run can leave a small follow-up for a person, or tick one off once it is done.
